reviews.diagnosis: The trio reads support a paternal HP1-to-HP2 switch in NA12879 within NA12877 phase set 19256651. Eight child reads carry G/G across the endpoints, four on each strand. Six also carry the paternal G allele at the upstream Mendelian anchor. The father has 17 G/A and 17 A/G spanning reads, and neither parent has a G/G spanning read at the audit thresholds. Extending the audit from 5 kb to 15 kb on either side found additional paternal HP2 markers. Two child reads link the endpoint G/G to paternal HP2 alleles at both 20,968,297 and 20,968,600. The supplied IGV overview shows reads spanning the interval. A phase-grouped view spanning the anchor and downstream markers would let me check the alignment context of the linked reads before finalizing.

The maternal VCF implies HP1-to-HP2 across the endpoints, but the right-hand maternal genotype has GQ 3 and the next informative marker at 21,166,076 implies HP1 again. All 26 eligible child reads and all 68 eligible paternal reads spanning both endpoints carry C/A. Eleven maternal reads also carry C/A across both maternal HP tags. Even with the upstream maternal-origin anchor and the downstream marker included, the same four-site pattern occurs in eight maternal-origin child reads, five maternal reads across both HP tags, and 20 paternal reads. The supplied IGV overview shows dense mismatches and alignment gaps around the locus. A tighter, phase-grouped view can test whether those alignment features account for the discordant maternal endpoint calls. The current reads leave the maternal switch unresolved.

The maternal left endpoint is unphased at GQ 9, and the phased flanking markers both imply maternal HP2. The three eligible maternal-origin child reads that span the endpoints carry C/C/A/A across the endpoints and the two flanking sites. Four maternal HP1-tagged reads and one paternal read already carry that same pattern. The ungrouped IGV overview shows all three read tracks across the interval. A phase-grouped view would let me check whether the maternal reads carrying the child pattern share a consistent local alignment and whether the maternal T allele at the left endpoint distinguishes a separate read group. The current evidence leaves the maternal switch unresolved.
